dedupe_resolutions.notes: The September 2 preliminary injunction changes the legal status of Executive Order 14418 and belongs in the existing birthright-citizenship record rather than a parallel court-ruling entry.
The closing ministerial consensus advances the previously recorded U.S. Carolina Principles proposal into an adopted nonbinding G20 framework; it is one policy sequence, not a second count.
Reuters' funding-scale and enforcement reporting materially clarifies the already-recorded DOJ state-reporting interpretation and is incorporated without a duplicate entry.
The September 2 remedies ruling follows the April 2025 liability judgment. This record covers the requested divestiture's rejection and ordered behavioral relief, not a second liability finding.
The September clinical guidance operationalizes the July directive. The entry groups announcement and implementation into one lifecycle record rather than counting them separately.

The records share a same-day White House fact sheet because it reports both manufacturer pricing arrangements and Medicare Bridge uptake. One is a set of announced company agreements; the other is an administration-reported program measurement.

The shared EO 14420 token is intentionally preserved in the grid record's timestamped correction note and source description. The official Federal Register assigns EO 14421 to the August 26 grid order and EO 14420 to the August 10 vaccine order; the records concern distinct events and subjects.
Both records arise from the U.S.-hosted G20 meetings but document distinct frameworks: innovation and AI governance versus trade responses to non-market export distortions.

rejected_candidates.title: Three new Truth Social posts
rejected_candidates.reason: The fallback advanced from 36,040 to 36,043 posts. One post was image-only, one linked opinion coverage about New York Attorney General Letitia James and one was personal praise. None independently established a qualifying federal action, evidence finding or policy change.

rejected_candidates.title: Justice Department work with X on attempted account-recovery attack
rejected_candidates.reason: The attorney general said DOJ was working with X after the platform disrupted an attempted password-recovery attack, but disclosed no charge, warrant, public filing, victim finding or material investigative detail. The existence of the statement is noted as a lead without converting a thin announcement into a canonical case record.

rejected_candidates.title: Maduro immunity dismissal motion
rejected_candidates.reason: The filing was made by a criminal defendant rather than the administration and did not produce a new executive action or court ruling. The prosecution and January capture remain distinct existing-event research leads pending the government's response and November hearing.

rejected_candidates.title: Campaign, travel-industry and ceremonial coverage
rejected_candidates.reason: Midterm campaign promises, meetings with travel executives, commemorative messages and similar events produced no signed instrument, implemented program, appropriation, ruling or measured result by cutoff.

rejected_candidates.title: Iran, Venezuela and trade forecasts
rejected_candidates.reason: Statements about future military, oil-production or trade steps did not establish another completed strike, signed instrument, disbursement or measured outcome beyond the existing records.

rejected_candidates.title: Anonymous-source and duplicate reports
rejected_candidates.reason: Consequential claims resting mainly on unnamed sources still lacked sufficient independent confirmation, while repeated accounts of already-recorded actions added no material evidence or lifecycle change.

rejected_candidates.title: External archive discovery leads
rejected_candidates.reason: Updated, unit-specific measurements remain separate discovery inputs and contribute zero canonical entries by default. No upstream archive item advanced without original-source inspection and full Record review.

corrections.summary: This release repairs three material September 2 omissions: the Google ad-tech remedies ruling, the Pentagon testosterone-screening guidance and the birthright-citizenship injunction. Their source publication times fell just before the prior boundary or during the preceding review window; they are labeled with their actual event dates and evidence status rather than presented as post-boundary actions.
